name: Rehoboam
bio:
Rehoboam was Solomon's son, who succeeded him as king after Solomon's forty-year reign ended and he was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 11:41-43).

Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king. Jeroboam, recalled from his exile in Egypt, came with the assembly and asked Rehoboam to lighten the heavy labor and taxation Solomon had placed on the people, promising their loyalty in return. Rehoboam asked for three days to consider, then rejected the advice of Solomon's experienced elders — who urged him to serve the people and win them over with kind words — in favor of the advice of the young men he had grown up with, who told him to answer harshly: "My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions." When Rehoboam gave this harsh answer, the assembled Israelites abandoned him on the spot, crying, "What share do we have in David... To your tents, Israel!" — all but the tribe of Judah rejected his rule. When Rehoboam sent Adoram, in charge of the forced labor, to try to enforce his authority, all Israel stoned him to death, and Rehoboam himself barely escaped to Jerusalem by chariot (1 Kings 12:1-19). Back in Jerusalem, Rehoboam assembled 180,000 soldiers from Judah and Benjamin to force the northern tribes back under his rule, but the LORD sent Shemaiah the man of God to tell him not to fight his own brothers, since the division was the LORD's doing; Rehoboam obeyed and the armies stood down (1 Kings 12:21-24). His reign, which saw the kingdom torn in two just as the prophet Ahijah had foretold to Jeroboam, continues to unfold in detail in the chapters ahead.
